To improve upon our earlier approximation, we compute the Green’s function to second order in $1/g$ . At this order, we obtain the following result:

$$ \displaystyle\overline{\lambda} \displaystyle=\frac{g^{2}}{4}+\frac{9}{4}, \displaystyle Q_{r}(\omega_{n}) \displaystyle=\frac{g}{\omega_{n}^{2}(1+3/g^{2})+(\overline{\lambda}-3)}, \displaystyle\Sigma_{r}(\tau) \displaystyle=\frac{3g^{5}}{2(g^{4}-9)}e^{-g|\tau|\sqrt{\frac{g^{2}-3}{g^{2}+3}}}, \displaystyle\Sigma_{r}(\omega_{n}) \displaystyle=\frac{3g^{6}}{\sqrt{g^{4}-9}}\frac{1}{g^{2}(g^{2}-3)+\omega_{n}^{2}(g^{2}+3)}. $$

We therefore conclude that at large $g$ , the spectral function has the form of a delta function

$$ \displaystyle\rho(\omega)=\frac{g^{3}}{g^{2}+3}\delta\left(\omega^{2}-\frac{g^{2}}{4}\frac{g^{2}-3}{g^{2}+3}\right), $$

with a finite gap. Thus, within this approximate framework, we expect the replica-symmetric solution to persist up to $g\approx\sqrt{3}$ .

## Appendix E Replica identities

We consider $n\times n$ replica matrices $A_{ab}$ whose off-diagonal elements are parametrized by the Parisi function $a(u)$ , $u\in[0,1]$ , and the diagonal element $A_{aa}=\tilde{a}$ (similarly for $B_{ab}$ and $C_{ab}$ ). We find it useful to define

$$ \displaystyle\langle a\rangle\equiv\int_{0}^{1}du\,a(u),\, $$

and

$$ \displaystyle[a](u)\equiv-\int_{0}^{u}dva(v)+ua(u)\,. $$

For the replica-symmetric case, we take

$$ \displaystyle a(u)=a,\quad\quad\tilde{a}=a+\sigma_{a}\,. $$

For the case of one-step replica symmetry breaking, we take

$$ \displaystyle\tilde{a} \displaystyle=a_{1}+\sigma_{a}, \displaystyle a(u) \displaystyle=\begin{cases}a_{1}\,,\quad\mbox{$x<u<1$}\\
a_{0}\,,\quad\mbox{$0<u<x$}\end{cases}. $$

Then, we have $\langle a\rangle=a_{1}-x(a_{1}-a_{0})$ , and

$$ \displaystyle[a](u)=\begin{cases}x(a_{1}-a_{0})\,,\quad&\mbox{$x<u<1$}\\
0\,,\quad&\mbox{$0<u<x$}\end{cases}. $$

We now present some useful identities for matrix operations in the limit $n\rightarrow 0$ .

### E.1 Term-by-term sum

$$ \frac{1}{n}\sum_{a,b=1}^{n}A_{ab}=\tilde{a}-\langle a\rangle. $$

### E.2 Matrix product

For

$$ C_{ab}=\sum_{c=1}^{n}A_{ac}B_{cb}\,, $$

we have [72]

$$ \displaystyle\tilde{c} \displaystyle=\tilde{a}\tilde{b}-\langle ab\rangle, \displaystyle c(u) \displaystyle=(\tilde{b}-\langle b\rangle)a(u)+(\tilde{a}-\langle a\rangle)b(u)-\int_{0}^{u}dv(a(u)-a(v))(b(u)-b(v)). $$

### E.3 Matrix inverse

To determine $B=A^{-1}$ , we set $C=1$ in the matrix product to obtain the relations

$$ \displaystyle 1 \displaystyle=\tilde{a}\tilde{b}-\langle ab\rangle, \displaystyle 0 \displaystyle=(\tilde{b}-\langle b\rangle)a(u)+(\tilde{a}-\langle a\rangle)b(u)-\int_{0}^{u}dv(a(u)-a(v))(b(u)-b(v)). $$

With replica-symmetric matrices, we have

$$ \displaystyle\sigma_{b} \displaystyle=\frac{1}{\sigma_{a}}, \displaystyle b \displaystyle=-\frac{a}{\sigma_{a}^{2}}. $$

For the case of one-step replica symmetry breaking, we have

$$ \displaystyle 1 \displaystyle=\tilde{a}\tilde{b}-a_{0}b_{0}x-a_{1}b_{1}(1-x), \displaystyle 0 \displaystyle=(\tilde{b}-b_{0}x-b_{1}(1-x))a_{0}+(\tilde{a}-a_{0}x-a_{1}(1-x))b_{0}, \displaystyle 0 \displaystyle=(\tilde{b}-b_{0}x-b_{1}(1-x))a_{1}+(\tilde{a}-a_{0}x-a_{1}(1-x))b_{1}-x(a_{1}-a_{0})(b_{1}-b_{0}). $$

Solving these equations, we obtain

$$ \displaystyle\sigma_{b} \displaystyle=\frac{1}{\sigma_{a}}, \displaystyle b_{1} \displaystyle=-\frac{a_{1}\sigma_{a}+x(a_{1}-a_{0})^{2}}{\sigma_{a}(\sigma_{a}+x(a_{1}-a_{0}))^{2}}, \displaystyle b_{0} \displaystyle=-\frac{a_{0}}{(\sigma_{a}+x(a_{1}-a_{0}))^{2}}. $$

### E.4 Term-by-term inverse sum

If $A^{-1}=B$ , then from (204)

$$ \displaystyle\frac{1}{n}\sum_{ab}A^{-1}_{ab}=\tilde{b}-\langle b\rangle. $$

From (207), we have

$$ \displaystyle 1 \displaystyle=\tilde{a}\tilde{b}-\langle ab\rangle, \displaystyle 0 \displaystyle=(\tilde{b}-\langle b\rangle)\langle a\rangle+(\tilde{a}-\langle a\rangle)\langle b\rangle-\langle ab\rangle+\langle a\rangle\langle b\rangle. $$

Taking the difference, we obtain

$$ \displaystyle\frac{1}{n}\sum_{ab}A^{-1}_{ab}=\frac{1}{\tilde{a}-\langle a\rangle}. $$

### E.5 Term-by-term product

For the product

$$ D_{ab}=\sum_{c,d=1}^{n}A_{ac}B_{db}\,, $$

we use the fact that $\sum_{c}A_{ac}$ is independent of the index $a$ for replica matrices. This yields a replica-symmetric matrix $D_{ab}$ , which is of independent $a,b$ and using (204) we have

$$ \displaystyle\tilde{d}=d(u)=(\tilde{a}-\langle a\rangle)(\tilde{b}-\langle b\rangle). $$

For the replica-symmetric case, $\tilde{d}=d=\sigma_{a}\sigma_{b}$ , and $\sigma_{d}=0$ . With one-step replica symmetry breaking $\tilde{d}=d_{0}=d_{1}=(\sigma_{a}+x(a_{1}-a_{0}))(\sigma_{b}+x(b_{1}-b_{0}))$ , and $\sigma_{d}=0$ .

### E.6 Trace log

The trace log is needed in the computation of the free energy. We have [72]

$$ \displaystyle\frac{1}{n}\mbox{Tr}\ln A=\ln(\tilde{a}-\langle a\rangle)+\frac{a(0)}{\tilde{a}-\langle a\rangle}-\int_{0}^{1}\frac{du}{u^{2}}\ln\frac{\tilde{a}-\langle a\rangle-[a](u)}{\tilde{a}-\langle a\rangle}\,. $$

In the replica-symmetric case, we have

$$ \displaystyle\frac{1}{n}\mbox{Tr}\ln A=\ln(\sigma_{a})+\frac{a}{\sigma_{a}}\,. $$

With one-step replica symmetry breaking, we have

$$ \displaystyle\frac{1}{n}\mbox{Tr}\ln A=\ln(\sigma_{a})+\frac{a_{0}}{\sigma_{a}+x(a_{1}-a_{0})}-\frac{1}{x}\ln\frac{\sigma_{a}}{\sigma_{a}+x(a_{1}-a_{0})}\,. $$

Let us now consider $\mbox{Tr}\ln(A+B)$ , where $B$ is a constant matrix, i.e., $\tilde{b}=b(u)=b$ , and $\sigma_{b}=0$ . Then, we have

$$ \displaystyle\frac{1}{n}\mbox{Tr}\ln(A+B)=\frac{1}{n}\mbox{Tr}\ln A+\frac{b}{\tilde{a}-\langle a\rangle}. $$

### E.7 Cubic term

According to (3.72) in Ref. 48, for the matrix $q_{ab}$ with $\tilde{q}=0$ ,

$$ \displaystyle\frac{1}{n}\mbox{Tr}q^{3}=\int_{0}^{1}du\left[u[q(u)]^{3}+3q(u)\int_{0}^{u}dv[q(v)]^{2}\right]. $$
